title: A structured decision template for tumour boards: a pragmatic trial across a six-hospital cancer network
subtitle: Pragmatic trial using the network's six-wave rollout of a structured decision template
statement: Across 11 tumour boards in six hospitals, only 54 percent of sampled case discussions documented all seven core decision items, with patient preferences recorded in 31 percent and the reason for departing from the guideline in 41 percent. Incomplete minutes are linked to longer waits for first treatment and to patients hearing different plans. A structured template with board coordinators and monthly feedback will reach every board in six waves during 2027, and the network needs a pragmatic trial within that rollout to show whether documentation improves and treatment starts sooner without longer meetings.
whoAffected: Patients whose cases are discussed at the 11 boards (about 18,000 a year), their families, the clinicians who act on board decisions, board chairs and coordinators.
whatHurts: Plans that cannot be read from the minutes, conflicting messages to patients, repeat discussions and delays to first treatment.
currentPractice: Free-text minutes typed by whoever is minuting, with no structure, no coordinator and no feedback.
whyNow: The rollout schedule, coordinator funding and ethics approval are in place, and the design must be approved in November 2026.
constraints: Six-wave rollout from February to December 2027 with all boards live by the end of 2027; three data-manager days a month; no research budget; board-level switch-on without blinding; an information system merger in mid-2027; short multilingual patient measures; design approval in November 2026.
patientCenteredGoal: Every patient discussed at a tumour board has a clear, agreed plan that their treating team can read and that they understand.
summary: Problem framed as a pragmatic trial within a staged network rollout; the reply condenses the constraints.
